description: U.S. Hazards Outlook is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA National Weather Service, Climate Prediction Center. Emergency managers and planners can get advance notice of potential hazards related to climate, weather, and hydrological events: these outlook maps highlight areas that may be impacted by hazards related to precipitation, temperature, wind, and drought during Week 2, the period spanning 8 to 14 days from now, according to scientists at NOAA's Climate Prediction Center. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, High Winds, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Critical Facilities, People, Property, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
